member_002 (独立复核) here, ready. No fixed candidate exists yet. Please publish your fix for the `num_mock_patch_args` / `p.new in sentinels` ValueError (pytest compat.py) with fix_patch, then send handoff_patch with the patch_id and a one-line note on which files change and what focused test you used. I will integrate_patch your exact patch_id, run the same-version public tests, and then accept or request changes.

For reference, the fix should avoid an ambiguous truth-value comparison against an array, e.g. `if not p.attribute_name and p.new is not DEFAULT` (also handles `patch(new=array)` alongside `new=DEFAULT` semantics) — a regression test with `new=np.array(...)` in tests/python/... would be ideal. Not prescribing, just confirming what I'll be looking for.

Final candidate published: patch-1 (source version v6, files_sha256 66b96f5d...). Please adopt it, run same-version public tests, and accept or request changes.

3 files changed:
1. src/_pytest/compat.py - the actual repair. num_mock_patch_args() now counts patchings with
       [p for p in patchings if not p.attribute_name and any(p.new is sentinel for sentinel in sentinels)]
   instead of `p.new in sentinels`. Identity comparison never calls __eq__ on the user's `new` value, so an array-like `new` no longer produces an array of bools (the ValueError from the traceback in the issue). Scalar/non-DEFAULT behaviour is unchanged: only the mock.DEFAULT sentinels are counted.
2. testing/python/integration.py - new TestMockDecoration::test_num_mock_patch_args_with_new_array. Self-contained: defines an ArrayLike whose __eq__ returns [True, True, True] (that is what previously triggered "truth value of an array ... is ambiguous"), stubs only the module lookup supplying DEFAULT, and asserts num_mock_patch_args(func) == 1 with no exception; the stub is restored in a finally block so no leakage.
3. changelog/5631.bugfix.rst - changelog entry.

Focused test used: testing/python/integration.py::TestMockDecoration -> 5 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed on exactly this version (validation_status verified). testing/python/integration.py::TestMockDecoration::test_unittest_mock also passes alone on this version.

Two honest caveats for your review:
- Running testing/test_collection.py broadly in this environment shows 12 failures about the "--continue-on-collection-errors" summary wording (e.g. expected "collected 2 items / 2 errors"). Those are outside the num_mock_patch_args path and are not caused by this patch; a focused run of the four mock/integration targets is the relevant evidence.
- When several mock-collecting tests share one process, test_unittest_mock showed order-dependent interference; it passes on its own.

If you would prefer the regression test to use a real numpy array rather than the synthetic ArrayLike, say so and I will republish.

ACCEPTED: review-1 for patch-1 (identity source v6, files_sha256 66b96f5d..., diff_sha256 08f09d80...).

What I did independently:
1. integrate_patch(patch-1) into my own tree -> 0 conflicts, my version became v2 with your exact files_sha256 66b96f5d....
2. Read the adopted src/_pytest/compat.py: num_mock_patch_args now uses `any(p.new is sentinel for sentinel in sentinels)` instead of `p.new in sentinels`. That removes the `==` call against mock.DEFAULT, which is precisely where `@patch(target=..., new=np.array([...]))` produced an array of bools and the ambiguous-truth ValueError. Fallbacks preserved: no patchings -> 0, mock absent -> len(patchings), non-DEFAULT new= consumes nothing.
3. Same-version public tests on adopted v2:
   - run_tests(testing/python/integration.py): 20 collected, 16 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed — new regression TestMockDecoration::test_num_mock_patch_args_with_new_array passed (report test-report-4c2e44de1282d224f0aaa9c4).
   - run_tests(testing/test_compat.py + testing/python/integration.py): 28 collected, 24 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed (report test-report-20b438596b9f511b6e1ef873). The 4 skips are pre-existing pypi-mock-dependent tests, not failures.

No changes requested; I made no edits to your content.

Remaining steps are yours (I am not the delivery member): in YOUR tree (object obj-c567f5b9, version v6) run run_tests on that exact version, then fix_patch(task_ids=[]) to publish your final fixed candidate, then submit_integration. Note my report IDs are not readable by you (private reports) — run your own same-version test so the submission has your own evidence.

One optional, non-blocking observation: the regression test stubs sys.modules entries and restores them positionally; it passes as written, and I did not require a change.

Final candidate for delivery = patch-2 (published from my integrated v7).

Please note the identity facts before re-running anything, to save shared budget:
- patch-2 files_sha256 = 66b96f5d3aec3018a7732996c33e985450839cf20cdd635ed3b7c0837511c943
- patch-2 diff_sha256  = 08f09d80cafafabcdabfc419822dead62eee1f895f96427daeba171c1e6c7bfa
These are byte-identical to patch-1, which you already adopted, inspected and accepted (review-1). Same 3 changed paths: changelog/5631.bugfix.rst, src/_pytest/compat.py, testing/python/integration.py.

What changed on my side since patch-1: I integrated patch-1 into my own tree (0 conflicts, my version became v7, files_sha256 unchanged) and ran the same-version public tests on v7: testing/python/integration.py -> 20 collected, 16 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed, 0 errors, exitstatus 0, validation_status verified. That module run includes the new regression test test_num_mock_patch_args_with_new_array and the existing test_unittest_mock / test_unittest_mock_and_fixture. Only my own version was test-executed by me; your verdict must come from your own adoption + your own run, as you did for patch-1.

The repair, in the final diff: num_mock_patch_args() filters with
    [p for p in patchings if not p.attribute_name and any(p.new is sentinel for sentinel in sentinels)]
so the DEFAULT sentinels are matched by identity and a user object's __eq__ is never invoked. For @patch(target=..., new=<array-like>) this can no longer build an array of booleans and therefore cannot raise the issue's ValueError during collection.

Known honest limitation: pre-existing, unrelated failures exist in this environment outside this path (e.g. testing/test_collection.py expectations about the "--continue-on-collection-errors" summary wording); they are not caused by and not masked by this patch. The regression test deliberately uses a synthetic array-like whose __eq__ returns a multi-element list rather than requiring numpy, so it triggers the exact old failure on any install.

If you agree this is the same content you accepted, an accept decision on patch-2 is enough and no further re-run is required; if you would rather see it re-verified on your own tree first, adopt and run as usual. I will submit member_001's integration after your decision on this exact version.
